steps.body: A **complex number** mixes both kinds: **a + bi**, with real part a and imaginary part b. Since it takes two numbers to describe, it lives on a **plane**: real part along the horizontal axis, imaginary part up the vertical. 3 + 2i is the point 3 right, 2 up.

widget.prompt: What is the REAL part of 4 − 7i?

options.feedback: Right — the standalone number is the real part; −7 rides with the i.
−7 is the IMAGINARY part (the coefficient of i) — the real part is 4.
The imaginary coefficient is −7, and either way it belongs to i — the real part is 4.

options.label: −7i
options.feedback: −7i is the whole imaginary TERM; the real part is the plain 4.

steps.body: Special positions: a purely **real** number like 5 sits ON the horizontal axis (its b is 0); a purely **imaginary** one like 5i sits ON the vertical axis (its a is 0). Every other complex number floats off both axes.

explanationVariants: 3 + 2i means real part 3 (right) and imaginary part 2 (up): the point (3, 2i).
Real part sets the horizontal position, imaginary part the vertical.

widget.prompt: Plot the complex number 3 + 2i on the plane (real axis across, imaginary axis up).

pointErrors.feedback: That's 2 + 3i — the REAL part 3 goes across, and the imaginary 2 goes up: (3, 2i).

widget.missFeedback: Move 3 along the real axis, then 2 up the imaginary axis.
widget.successFeedback: Right — 3 + 2i lives at 3 across, 2 up, exactly like the figure.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents complex plane.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for complex plane must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines complex plane.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: Who lives on the vertical axis?

widget.prompt: Which number sits ON the imaginary (vertical) axis?

options.label: 5i
options.feedback: Right — its real part is 0, so it has no horizontal offset.
5 is purely real — it sits on the HORIZONTAL axis, imaginary part 0.

options.label: 3 + i
options.feedback: With real part 3, it floats 3 units off the vertical axis.
−2 is purely real — on the horizontal axis, just left of center.

explanationVariants: The imaginary part is the bare coefficient b — for 6 + 5i, that's 5.
Convention: 'imaginary part' means the real number multiplying i.

widget.prompt: What is the IMAGINARY part of 6 + 5i?

options.feedback: Right — the imaginary part is the coefficient of i, a plain real number.

options.label: 5i
options.feedback: 5i is the imaginary TERM — the imaginary PART is just its coefficient, 5.
6 is the real part; the imaginary part rides with the i: 5.
6 + 5 merges the two parts — they stay separate: real 6, imaginary 5.

explanationVariants: 1 + 4i: real part 1 across, imaginary part 4 up.
The small real part keeps it near the vertical axis, high up.

pointErrors.feedback: That's 4 + i — swapped parts. The real 1 goes ACROSS and the 4 goes UP: (1, 4i).

widget.missFeedback: Real part 1 across, imaginary part 4 up.
widget.successFeedback: Right — 1 + 4i sits close to the imaginary axis, four units up.

explanationVariants: 2 right means real part 2; 5 up means imaginary part 5: the number is 2 + 5i.
Horizontal position names a, vertical names b, and the number is a + bi.

widget.prompt: A point sits 2 units right and 5 units up. Which complex number is it?

options.label: 5 + 2i
options.feedback: That swaps the axes — 5 + 2i sits 5 RIGHT and 2 up. Across is real: 2 + 5i.

options.label: 2 − 5i
options.feedback: −5i would point 5 units DOWN — this point is above the real axis: 2 + 5i.

options.label: −2 + 5i
options.feedback: Real part −2 sits 2 units LEFT — this point is to the right: 2 + 5i.

hints: The horizontal position is the real part.
The vertical position is the imaginary part's size.

steps.body: a + bi is a point: real part across, imaginary part up.
takeaways: Real part a and imaginary part b are both plain real numbers.
Purely real numbers live on the horizontal axis; purely imaginary on the vertical.
The imaginary PART of a + bi is b, not bi.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: arithmetic — adding, multiplying, and dividing these new numbers.

concept.body: In a + bi, the real part is the standalone a. For 9 + 3i, the real part is 9.

explanationVariants: 3 belongs to the i; the free-standing 9 is the real part.

widget.prompt: What is the REAL part of 9 + 3i?

commonErrors.feedback: 3 is the IMAGINARY part (the coefficient of i) — the real part is 9.
9 + 3 merges the parts — they never combine: the real part is 9.

widget.fallbackFeedback: The standalone number is the real part: 9.
